unit.name: AI hiring reset and strategic opportunity
unit.description: Laurence introduces the AI job-market landscape, including slower junior hiring, high-profile layoffs, overhiring history, and the need to approach opportunities strategically.
unit.summary: Laurence begins by telling students to use the networks and prestige available to them because the current job landscape is difficult [ts=1440s]. He names signals such as junior hiring slowdown, high-profile layoffs, scarce-feeling entry-level positions, and fierce competition, but answers that students should not simply worry [ts=1512s]. His explanation links the current market to pandemic-era slowdown, 2022-2023 overhiring, and a 2024-2025 correction in which companies became more cautious about AI claims [ts=1604s]. The actionable message is that opportunity remains large for people who understand the changing industry and approach job search strategically [ts=1739s].

key_points.text: Students are advised to use the Stanford network and prestige because the current landscape is not ideal.
Junior hiring is described as slowing while layoffs and competition dominate the signals students see.
The 2022-2023 period is described as a time of AI-driven and post-pandemic overhiring.
The 2024-2025 adjustment made companies more cautious about AI skills on resumes.
Opportunity remains for candidates who approach the AI landscape strategically.
